title: Immaculate Constellation USAP set up in 2017 to sequester overhead UAP data

tellings.quote: So, a program like Immaculate Constellation or a legacy program satellite because Immaculate Constellation isn't a legacy program. It was a it was a reactionary US app established in 2017 would clip out data that would probably depict anomalies like a UFO and sequester it into MCOM or another legacy program site.

plain: A secret Pentagon program called Immaculate Constellation was set up in 2017, in reaction to UFO news going public, to pull UFO images out of satellite and other overhead data and hide them away in a site he calls MCOM or in an older secret program, says a researcher who goes by UAPGerb, telling Michels this himself without naming a source; if true, it would explain why so few in the military ever see such images. The program's only public trace is the Immaculate Constellation report, an unsigned paper entered into the record of a congressional hearing on 13 November 2024 that a former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote, and the Defense Department says it has no record of such a program. The report says the program was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", small Pentagon efforts that studied UFO reports, draws on platforms "in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the upper atmosphere" and below, and works by "detecting, quarantining, and transferring UAP and RV imagery collection incidents before they are circulated", which matches his clipping of data, while the year 2017 is his reading of "following".

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says the program was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", draws on platforms "in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the upper atmosphere" and below, and "enforces compartmentalization by detecting, quarantining, and transferring UAP and RV imagery collection incidents before they are circulated". It dates the program only as after the 2017 disclosure, so UAPGerb's founding year of 2017 is his reading of "following"; the clipping of overhead data corresponds to the report's quarantining of collection incidents.
